title: Joint re-issue candidate of CP-01 (revision 3) and CP-02: one verifiable candidate, nothing adopted
adoption: Order 19B only, with the owner's explicit approval of that PR at that SHA (gate OWNER_SIGNATURE_AND_ADOPTION, merge policy OWNER_EXPLICIT_PER_PR). This candidate adopts, activates, re-issues and signs nothing.

records.carries: the state of every CP-01 item (column 'In the proposal')
the class Order 17 recorded for every CP-02 item (section 3) and the empty owner's decision block (section 8)

applyOrder: CP-01's items in their order, then CP-02's items in their order: CP-02 requires CP-01 (README of docs/authority/proposals, adoption step 2; CP-02 section 7.2). A profile applies the same ops of its items in the same order and skips the others; appends land in that order.

adoption.meaning: The most Order 19B may adopt: items whose substance is decided. Each still needs its CP-02 owner's decision (CP-02 items), the owner's approval of the Order 19B PR, and every condition below satisfied, or it stays out.

build.meaning: The contract the implementing orders build and test against with the activation off by default: the adoption items plus the CONDITIONAL ones (principle and values decided, adoption blocked by a named condition). Never adopted as a whole: a CONDITIONAL item enters a re-issue only once its pending list is empty.

conflicts.resolution: Cases are found by id, never by position; ids are unique (CP02-nn-tag and the commands' OK/DENY/RACE). The apply order fixes their positions; a profile that leaves an item out simply does not append its cases.

Commands are found by id (CMD065 to CMD081, each owned by one item); CP-02.21's and CP-02.19's text changes test existing commands by their base index, which an append never moves. Leaving an item out leaves a gap in the CMD numbers, never a renumbering.

Contracts are found by name; names are unique across both proposals and the registry (the generator refuses a duplicate). CP-02.10 extends CommissionStatement through its base index, which no append moves. Each profile's generated bundle is proved to define every contract its operations answer.
Case ids added to a gate's list; each item first tests the gate's id at its base index. Order inside the list carries no meaning; the profile adds only its items' ids.

SellerRecordView.why: CP-02.08 names its owner-only read of one seller (seller, agreement, customers, statements, claims) after a new registry contract SellerRecordView; the served api already has a component SellerRecordView, B10's owner-tools record of a seller's onboarding, assignment or termination (packages/application/src/commercial/sellers/owner-tools). CP-02.openapi.json is a document of its own, so the clash never showed there; one served document cannot hold both. The registry contract keeps its name (x-kauro-schema-id stays urn:kauro:r2:contracts#/$defs/SellerRecordView); the component the implementing order serves takes the candidate's name or another free one.

SupportCasePage.why: CP-02.03's ListAgencySupportCases answers a page of the registry contract SupportCase, which CP-02's generator names SupportCasePage; the served api already has SupportCasePage, the page of one project's cases (ListSupportCases, items SupportCaseView, oldest first). The workspace-wide page is a different list (newest first, cursor bound to the agency), so it takes its own name.

adoptionGates: The owner's explicit approval of the Order 19B PR at its SHA (OWNER_EXPLICIT_PER_PR); the general technical authorization GA-2026-10-22 does not cover adoption.
For each CP-02 item, the owner's decision in CP-02 section 8 (empty today): Order 17 classed fifteen items approved on earlier decisions, and CP-02 section 7.1 makes that block the adoption act.
Only items of the adoption profile, each with the items it requires or depends on, and each with every condition below satisfied with evidence; any other item stays out and keeps its state.

Not the adoption profile wholesale: CP-01.02 and CP-02.04 (elevated retention) and CP-01.04, CP-01.14 and CP-02.14 (PENDING_COUNSEL) fall under Order 19B's own exclusions and are adoptable only after the condition o19bExclusions names (the legal procedure for LR-01 and O21; the competent review of the claim rules); an item that requires one of them is held with it (CP-02.02 requires CP-01.02; CP-02.12 requires CP-01.14).

The candidate is current on the SHA Order 19B starts from (node tools/reissue/reissue.mjs check); if a proposal, the registry, the served api or a generated consumer moved, the candidate is regenerated and reviewed again first.

In the same change (README adoption steps 2 to 4): the new edition label, PROVENANCE source and hashes; @kauro/contracts regenerated; every copy of a changed value with its drift test; the web client regenerated with the server for each coordinated change; the registry's own test counts updated; adopted items moved to ADOPTED and checked against the registry by the proposal tests.
